subject: Staged compatibility upgrade: VPC maintenance windows & rollback gating
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: ops@greenlinehealth.com, chloe_martin@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-20T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Staged compatibility upgrade: VPC maintenance windows & rollback gating

Hi team,

Following our run-of-call last week, attaching a compact rollout proposal for Greenline's private deployment. High-level goals: preserve pinned model versions for sensitive tenants, run a three-step canary (control plane-only, single-region canary, cross-region canary), and validate network config changes on a non-prod mirror before any VPC route updates.

Key asks for Greenline ops: please propose one 3-hour maintenance window (UTC offsets below) in the next two weeks where you can accept ephemeral routing changes and a brief KV-cache eviction. We will not unpin versions during the canary; unpinning is its own separate change.

Tollgates (pass/fail checks) we intend to gate on:
- Successful canary traffic match within 2% of baseline latency and 1% of error rate
- No auth/audit regressions from your side (SOC2 evidence collector will run after each slice)
- Network routes validated on mirrored subnets, then applied to canary subnets only

I've attached: redwood-staged-rollout-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook + rollback checklist), netplan-change-diff.patch (proposed netmask / route delta), and a preliminary canary schedule.

If Greenline signs off on the window and can confirm a primary on-call for the day, we'll lock the exact sequence and share an ops bridge link and DocuSign approval for the maintenance.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-staged-rollout-runbook-v1.pdf (PDF, 1.8MB); netplan-change-diff.patch (text); canary-window-schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Greenline Health Ops <ops@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: chloe_martin@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-20T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Staged compatibility upgrade: VPC maintenance windows & rollback gating

Marissa — thanks for the clear plan and the docs. A couple quick clarifications from our infra team before we pick a window:

1) How long will the ephemeral route stay active on the canary subnets? We prefer routes that can be reverted in <10 minutes if health checks fail.
2) You mentioned not unpinning versions — what is the expected maximum pinned duration post-upgrade? Our change control requires a defined sunset date for any temporary pins.
3) Will your KV-cache eviction be a full global flush or per-tenant prefix? We need to ensure our downstream storage retention and backup windows aren't impacted.

Suggested maintenance windows (PST): 2026-05-03 02:00–05:00, 2026-05-06 01:00–04:00. Both are low-traffic nights for us.

We can have Neal (on-call network lead) on the bridge.

— GL Ops

Folks — answering GL Ops questions and adding technical constraints:

1) Ephemeral route duration: we'll program the BGP announcement to be applied to canary subnets only, with an automated withdraw timer of 6 minutes. Manual abort will withdraw immediately; we recommend the 10-minute abort SLA as a safety envelope, but the automation withdraw is 6 minutes by default.

2) Pin window: for this upgrade the plan is to pin the tenant-specific model variant at the current SHA for 72 hours post-successful cross-region canary. After 72 hours we'll propose auto-rollover testing to the next minor (hotfix) build — but we will only change that with explicit signoff from Greenline. We'll add the pin-expiry timestamp in DocuSign before the maintenance window.

3) KV-cache eviction: per-tenant prefix only. We will target the tenant prefixes impacted by the canary and do progressive prefix eviction to avoid a global cold start. This will be scripted in the runbook (see redwood-staged-rollout-runbook-v1.pdf) and logged to your audit endpoint.

Also: netplan-change-diff.patch contains only the canary-range route and a single ACL tweak for the telemetry subnet — no changes to customer-facing firewall policies. I attached a compact patch for ops to run in a test mirror before applying to canaries.

Connor — can you add a short checklist for the SOC evidence collector step (audit log export, tamper check, and retention confirmation)? I can include it in the runbook before we circulate for signing.

— Ben

Hi Neal / GL Ops,

Thanks for the candidate windows — both look workable. I've converted them into the attached schedule (canary-window-schedule.xlsx) and added the bridge details and expected checkpoints per hour. Short summary of the timeline we propose for the 3-hour slot:

Hour 0–0:30: pre-bridge checks, snapshot backups (control-plane + KV snapshot), doc verification
Hour 0:30–1:15: control-plane canary (no route changes, rollout of new binaries to canary hosts)
Hour 1:15–2:15: network canary (apply route to canary subnets, progressive traffic shift up to 10%)
Hour 2:15–2:45: cross-region canary (if network metrics OK, apply to second region canary)
Hour 2:45–3:00: stabilize and decision: promote or rollback

Abort criteria (immediate rollback):
- 2x baseline latency increase for >5 minutes
- 1% sustained 5xx increase
- Any authentication/authorization failures observed in audit reports

We will ask for signed DocuSign by EOD 2026-04-22 to lock the 2026-05-03 window; if we don't have a signature we'll fall back to 2026-05-06.

Marissa — Ben mentioned adding the SOC evidence checklist. Connor, can you drop that checklist by EOD? I'll fold it into the runbook and re-upload.

Thanks,
Chloe
Program Manager, Private Deployments

Chloe / Marissa — we've reviewed the attachments and the updated schedule. Neal confirmed the automated withdraw timer and is comfortable with the per-tenant eviction plan after Ben's notes. Two small asks before we sign:

1) Add a line in the runbook documenting the exact S3 path and retention key for the KV snapshots so our compliance team can reconcile backups.
2) Add a patch rollback command (single-line) that our on-call can execute from the bridge — we prefer an ops-runbook snippet we can copy to our runbook.

If you add those two lines and re-upload, we can route the DocuSign mirror and sign for the 2026-05-03 02:00–05:00 PST window. We'll have Neal on the bridge and will CC our security reviewer during the canary.
